nary_nodes.label: Climate change reshaping Africa's malaria risk
evidence: How climate change is reshaping Africa's malaria risk
Climate change is not only heating up the continent, it's redistributing risks, says Olugbenga Mokuolu, professor of pediatrics at Nigeria's University of Ilorin.
Climate change is fundamentally changing the geography of disease on the continent, Olumide Idowu, founder of the International Climate Change Development Initiative, told DW.
nary_nodes.type_definition: An event or ongoing process that alters the nature or distribution of a specific risk.
nary_nodes.type_justification: None of the candidates capture the specific concept of 'reshaping' or altering a risk; they are too specific or outdated event types. 'Event' is the required parent.

nary_nodes.label: WHO warned funding cuts jeopardizing malaria control
evidence: The WHO warned in April 2025 that recent funding cuts were jeopardising malaria control efforts, with more than half of malaria-endemic countries surveyed reporting moderate or severe disruptions to malaria services.

nary_nodes.label: Lancet study found vaccine reduced mortality
evidence: A study published in The Lancet found that the RTS,S/AS01 malaria vaccine reduced all-cause mortality among vaccine-eligible children by 13.2% in pilot programs in Ghana, Kenya and Malawi.

nary_nodes.label: Nature study on temperature and malaria transmission
evidence: Malaria transmission is most efficient within temperature ranges common across many tropical regions of West and Central Africa, according to a new study published in the journal Nature.

The Nature study found that rising temperatures are making parts of southern Africa and high-elevation areas of East Africa increasingly suitable for malaria transmission, while parts of West Africa are becoming too hot for optimal transmission.

nary_nodes.label: Climate change redistributes malaria risks
evidence: Climate change is not only heating up the continent, it's redistributing risks, says Olugbenga Mokuolu, professor of pediatrics at Nigeria's University of Ilorin.
How climate change is reshaping Africa's malaria risk

nary_nodes.label: World too hot for malaria not good for children
evidence: Although West African countries like Nigeria fall under areas that are "too hot for malaria to thrive, this is not good news to celebrate either, because a world that's too hot for malaria is not a good world for children's health overall," Mokuolu, who also serves as an advisor to the Nigerian Minister of Health on malaria elimination, told DW.

nary_nodes.label: Heat dangerous for people
evidence: "The same heat that's inconvenient for mosquitoes is dangerous for people," he added, noting that climate is "not the primary driving factor of malaria.

nary_nodes.label: Climate not primary malaria driving factor
evidence: "The same heat that's inconvenient for mosquitoes is dangerous for people," he added, noting that climate is "not the primary driving factor of malaria. Funding, drug and insecticide resistance, and health system strength still matter more."

nary_nodes.label: Malaria elimination story of two regions
evidence: Olugbenga continued that the elimination and prevention of malaria on the continent could become "a story of two very different regions: West and Central Africa may get a small, unplanned assist from climate, while East and Southern Africa, historically lower-burden areas, face a growing new threat that could undo hard-won gains."

nary_nodes.label: Climate change changing disease geography
evidence: Climate change is fundamentally changing the geography of disease on the continent, Olumide Idowu, founder of the International Climate Change Development Initiative, told DW.

nary_nodes.label: Adaptation plan implementation lagged
evidence: Idowu added that many African countries have developed adaptation plans but implementation has lagged behind the pace of climate change.

nary_nodes.label: Africa vulnerable to climate change
evidence: Although Africa is one of the lowest contributors to greenhouse gas emissions, it remains one of the most vulnerable regions to climate change — posing systemic threats to the economy, infrastructure, and even its fragile health systems.

nary_nodes.label: African countries risk unpreparedness
evidence: Idowu mentioned that without a significant increase in "investment at home, reinforcement of local institutional capacity and embedding health as a core pillar of climate resilience, many African countries risk being unprepared for the changing epidemiological landscape that climate change is creating."

nary_nodes.label: Hardest hit regions less accustomed to fighting malaria
evidence: The regions expected to be hardest hit are also regions less accustomed to fighting malaria today, the study revealed.

nary_nodes.label: Adapt to evolving threat
evidence: "Governments, health systems and communities must adapt to this evolving threat, including getting ready now to run more aggressive anti-malaria programs in cooler areas where risk is rising," Olugbenga said.

nary_nodes.label: Sustain malaria elimination efforts
evidence: He also urged countries in West and Central Africa to sustain malaria elimination efforts, warning that resistance to insecticides and drugs, funding gaps and weak health systems could easily negate any reduction in malaria transmission associated with rising temperatures.

nary_nodes.label: Rising temperatures make Southern/East Africa suitable for malaria
evidence: The Nature study found that rising temperatures are making parts of southern Africa and high-elevation areas of East Africa increasingly suitable for malaria transmission
